title: Quiz: Atomic Number and Mass Number

questions.stem: What does the atomic number (Z) of an element represent?

options.text: The total number of protons and neutrons
The number of protons in the nucleus
The number of neutrons in the nucleus
The total number of electrons and protons

questions.explanation: The atomic number (Z) is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom. It uniquely defines the element and is also called the proton number.

questions.stem: In atomic notation, where is the mass number written?

options.text: To the right of the symbol
After the element name
At the top left of the symbol
At the bottom left of the symbol

questions.explanation: In atomic notation, the mass number (A) is written at the top left and the atomic number (Z) at the bottom left of the chemical symbol.

questions.stem: An aluminium atom has an atomic number of 13 and a mass number of 27. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 27 - 13 = 14. The aluminium atom has 13 protons and 14 neutrons in its nucleus.

questions.stem: Why is the atomic number always smaller than the mass number (for elements other than hydrogen-1)?

options.text: Because atomic number measures charge, not particles
Because atoms always have more electrons than protons
Because the mass number includes both protons and neutrons, while the atomic number counts only protons
Because neutrons are heavier than protons

questions.explanation: The mass number (A) is the total of protons plus neutrons, while the atomic number (Z) counts only the protons. Since most atoms have at least one neutron, A is larger than Z.

questions.stem: Two atoms both have an atomic number of 17 but mass numbers of 35 and 37. Why are both classified as chlorine?

options.text: Because they have the same atomic number, meaning the same number of protons
Because they have the same number of neutrons
Because they have the same mass number
Because they have the same symbol Cl

questions.explanation: Both atoms have 17 protons. Since the number of protons defines the element, both are chlorine atoms. They have different mass numbers because they have different numbers of neutrons.

questions.stem: An atom of potassium has 19 protons and 20 neutrons. What is its mass number?
questions.explanation: Mass number = protons + neutrons = 19 + 20 = 39. The mass number represents the total number of nucleons in the nucleus.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about atomic number is correct?

options.text: Two different elements can share the same atomic number
The atomic number defines the element and does not change in chemical reactions
The atomic number is also known as the nucleon number
The atomic number can change during chemical reactions

questions.explanation: The atomic number defines the element and cannot change during chemical reactions. Changing the number of protons would change the element entirely, which only occurs in nuclear reactions.
